records.summary: The idea is to buy and grow downloadable software for a niche audience. Customers would receive the software as a file after paying once.
records.customer: A niche software audience; exact customer is not stated.

revenue_claims.claim: The business grew to about $4,000 a month.
An earlier stair-step business made five grand a month before Rob bought a SaaS.

rounds.plain: The revenue evidence is about 20 years old, and no niche or acquisition method is named. The source says this is too stale to support the idea.

risks: Revenue claims are not independently verified.
The niche and customer acquisition method are unspecified.

hours.note: Pipeline estimate; updates, support and customer discovery still need Ricardo.

records.next_steps: Recheck the original product’s market and acquisition path, plus current competition and AI substitutes.

records.summary: The idea is to sell reusable AI skill files that package niche expertise or workflows for Claude users and other AI power users. Examples include turning YouTube videos into SEO blog posts, designing thumbnails, and editing generic AI phrasing.
records.how_money: One-time digital-product sales through a creator website; another source suggests selling through an online marketplace, with no price stated.
records.customer: Claude and AI power users, including marketers and content creators.

revenue_claims.claim: The digital product had made over $3,000 passively.
The skill stack had made over $3,000.

records.paid_demand: A creator said the digital product had made over $3,000 passively shortly after launch. The creator had an existing audience; the source does not establish that the sales would transfer to a new seller.

competitors.name: Anthropic directory
competitors.note: The validation report says the directory is free-only.

rounds.plain: The skills are copyable markdown and the idea has no clear moat. The validation report also says it needs an audience.

risks: Sales evidence may depend on the creator’s existing audience.
Skills are easy to copy and marketplace discovery is uncertain.
records.moat: The validation report says there is no moat; skills are copyable markdown.

hours.note: Pipeline estimate; product quality and distribution still need human judgment.

records.next_steps: Recheck current Claude skill formats, marketplace availability and rules, and the cited creator’s sales context.

records.summary: A subscription API helps developers and product teams add social media publishing to their apps. Customers use the software and its integrations to publish to social platforms.
records.how_money: Monthly subscriptions, starting at $10/month, with higher tiers at $25, $50, and $100/month.
records.customer: Technical users, developers, and SaaS or product teams that want social posting integrations.

revenue_claims.claim: The business’s monthly recurring revenue exceeded the founder’s previous salary.
They started running Google Ads after crossing $10,000 in monthly recurring revenue.
MRR rose from $300 to $500, reaching $500 after five months.

records.paid_demand: The founder described a subscription business and said its MRR exceeded his previous salary. The source gives monthly subscription prices starting at $10/month.

competitors.name: Post for Me
competitors.note: Named in the validation report as a price comparison.

rounds.plain: The validation report cites a price war and dependence on social-platform APIs. Competition is strong, and customer acquisition is a hurdle.

risks: Dependence on social-platform API access and changes.
Customer acquisition and integration support require ongoing work.

hours.note: Pipeline estimate; platform changes and difficult support cases need oversight.

records.next_steps: Recheck current social-platform API access and rules, competitors, and the cited pricing.

records.summary: The idea is to send businesses automated weekly reports about up to three competitors’ Meta ads. A workflow would analyze the ads and email a formatted report on a schedule.
records.how_money: A proposed subscription of $300/month; this price is hypothetical in the source.
records.customer: Businesses that want to monitor competitors’ advertising.

revenue_claims.claim: The proposed service costs $300 per month and sends a weekly report on three competitors.

competitors.name: Rival Ads
competitors.note: The validation report says it already offers competitor-ad reports.

rounds.plain: The service is already productised by Rival Ads at $29/mo. The proposed $300 price is hypothetical, not evidence of paying demand.

risks: Demand and the proposed price are unverified.

hours.note: Pipeline estimate; sales, quality checks and support still need attention.

records.next_steps: Recheck Meta Ads Library access and terms, plus current Gumloop, Gemini and OpenAI capabilities and prices.

records.summary: The idea is a community analytics app for operators of online communities. The source does not describe its features or delivery in detail.
records.how_money: Recurring revenue is mentioned, but pricing and currency are not stated.
records.customer: Online community operators; exact customer segment is not stated.

revenue_claims.claim: Meatwaves reached 5K MRR; the currency is not stated.

records.paid_demand: The guest claimed Meatwaves reached 5K MRR, but the currency is not stated. The validation report names Statbot, ServerLens and free Discord Insights as alternatives.

competitors.name: Discord Insights
competitors.note: Named as a free alternative in the validation report.

rounds.plain: The validation report calls the category commoditised and names free and paid alternatives. The account says the product ‘never took off’.

risks: The revenue claim’s currency and operating details are missing.
The product, customer segment and acquisition route are not described in detail.

hours.note: Pipeline estimate; customer discovery, integrations and support remain human tasks.

records.next_steps: Recheck the exact customer niche, data access and platform integrations.

records.summary: The idea is a hosted web app for live-print and photo-magnet event vendors. Guests scan a QR code to upload and crop photos, pay, and send print-ready orders into a print queue.
records.customer: Photo-magnet and live-print event vendors, including the founder’s kit buyers.
records.paid_demand: The source describes a workflow improvement: one person can run an event station with the software. It does not state that customers pay for the app.

competitors.name: Vixie
competitors.note: Named in the validation report’s list of live competitors.

competitors.name: ReadyPix
competitors.note: Named in the validation report’s list of live competitors.

competitors.name: PrintBooth
competitors.note: Named in the validation report’s list of live competitors.

rounds.plain: The validation report says there are 6+ live competitors and the moat fails. The source also leaves willingness to pay unstated.

risks: Willingness to pay and licensing terms are unstated.
Vendor onboarding, printer edge cases and event-time support may require human work.

hours.note: Pipeline estimate; vendor acquisition, printer troubleshooting and timely support need human attention.

records.next_steps: Validate vendor demand, pricing, payment and print-workflow integrations before building around them.

records.summary: The idea is an app that lets users rewrite or translate text in different styles or languages. Users enter or speak text, choose a mode, and receive rewritten text.
records.how_money: Weekly or yearly subscriptions with trials; the speaker says a weekly plan performed better in this case.
records.customer: Students, non-English speakers, and people who want to rewrite text in a chosen style.

revenue_claims.claim: The app was making about $2,600 per month.
Downloads from the rankings were generating about $2,500 per month.

records.paid_demand: The speaker said the app was making about $2,600 per month and described weekly or yearly subscription plans with trials. The validation report names QuillBot and built-in rewrite tools as competing alternatives.

competitors.name: QuillBot
competitors.note: Named in the validation report as a competitor.

competitors.name: Built-in rewrite tools
competitors.note: The validation report names built-in tools as alternatives.

rounds.plain: The validation report calls this a commoditised feature, with QuillBot and built-in rewrite tools as alternatives. It also flags fast AI substitution and academic-integrity concerns.

risks: Strong competition and easy AI substitution.
The source describes a use case involving bypassing AI detection.
Revenue evidence is from one account and is not corroborated.

hours.note: Pipeline estimate; acquisition, support, quality checks and model-cost management need recurring attention.

records.next_steps: Recheck current model/API costs, App Store rules, ASO data, and subscription performance.
